principle: Store the minimum authored semantic poses and deterministic deformation parameters required to reconstruct motion; do not store generated bridge frames.
rules: Prefer idle plus one action extremum when those poses preserve the action identity; add a loading or contact pose only when deletion changes support, load, contact, facing, timing, or state understanding.
A default locomotion cycle may use run-oriented silhouettes at a deliberate jog cadence; do not force a walk vocabulary when the commissioned identity is a run.
Treat key exposure timing and deformation amplitude as independent axes. Once deformation is accepted, timing-only tuning must byte-preserve the deformation parameter block.
When continuous motion is requested, do not insert a static hold interval. Use a continuous bridge curve that returns to the clean authored pose at the instantaneous pose cut.

Bridge deformation may use whole-sprite balance stretch, squash, and shear around a ground-locked frame pivot, while secondary cloth and hose motion must be spatially localized away from the torso and planted foot.
Do not add root motion unless explicitly commissioned.
Identity authority remains the accepted alpha-cut source atlas and source rectangles; procedural motion must not replace or redraw authored poses.
Human visual acceptance on the deployed Sprite Lab surface is required before promotion. Tests and HTTP availability are necessary evidence, not visual acceptance.
Tune accepted timing in small increments without changing pose order, source identity, or deformation.
Use one reusable transparent RGBA atlas for the character; do not create per-animation duplicate sheets or projects.
A contact sheet may establish a coherent identity and pose family, but its cells become production keys only after exact topology and landmark review.
For a run, opposite stride states must visibly reverse leg ownership, hip rotation, torso counter-rotation, and arm swing; image alternation alone is not motion.
Do not substitute root translation for requested joint or limb motion.
If a segment is rigged, move the whole bone segment rigidly and localize deformation to the joint; proximity smearing is a rejected weighting model.
For a one-frame idle, keep the motion a bounded loop rather than a transient impulse: centered base, pinned feet, intentional cyclical skew, and phase-lagged secondary materials.
When upper-body motion reads top-heavy, add a localized opposed transfer between declared hip and knee anchor lines; keep both anchors, lower legs, and feet at zero displacement.
Distinguish intentional whole-body skew from damaging local warp. Preserve a good sway while reducing anatomical deformation.
Archive useful failures as named techniques with prohibited production uses instead of deleting them from the ledger.

Run an accepted-atlas preflight before any ImageGen call, new pose, contact sheet, rig, or interpolation experiment: enumerate relevant cells and motion programs, and reuse an accepted cell whenever it already carries the requested semantic state.

Never resolve a numeric cell/frame reference against a global project order. Bind production keys by source identity tuple: source sheet or atlas SHA-256, cell index, and semantic pose. For April, combat idle is 910948.png SHA-256 7e528cec4d32aed5077e7fbb1d90d0044a150d4251308a34d273ffc219d87a90 cell 0/top-left guarded stance; frame-0001-a95071a3 is ordinary upright idle and is not combat idle.

Honor the commissioned review surface exactly. For established April work, install the animation in the existing phone-hosted Sprite Lab / 2D Pose Lab V2 project and return that live route. Do not substitute GIF, video, offline preview, ChatGPT Site, or a new viewer unless explicitly requested.
If the commissioned phone review surface is not callable, fail closed at that boundary and preserve the accepted atlas/project unchanged; a substitute preview is not delivery.

Treat animations as append-only project history: snapshot the complete pre-mutation animation ID set and project hash; after mutation require every prior ID to remain and every untouched animation to remain byte-equivalent. Never delete an animation, including detector-created or rejected work; quarantine exact bytes outside the active loader. The live save surface must fail closed when the animation-ID set shrinks.

Bind every Sprite Lab review route to the saved project source SHA-256 and requested animation ID. An animation-only URL is insufficient because newest-upload automatic detection can open a different project and hide accepted clips.

Never derive sprite opacity globally from luminance, maximum channel, chroma, saturation, or any appearance feature when foreground materials can share the background color. For black-background JPEG contact sheets, identify background by tight border sampling plus border-connected flood fill; remove only the connected exterior matte, preserve all enclosed subject RGB as opaque, and restrict any feathering to the exterior boundary.

Before promoting an alpha-cut cell, composite it over checkerboard, mid-gray, and white; compare the frozen frame with the original source at inspection zoom. Fail if anatomy, dark armor, hair, cloth, line art, or neutral interior regions become transparent. Pixel-coordinate/hash correctness and RGB preservation do not prove alpha correctness.

When two accepted/on-model sprite sheets differ only in tint, prefer a deterministic post-grade over regeneration. Measure the palette from the exact accepted frame rectangles, not the whole atlas; modify only visible RGB in the mismatched source region; byte-preserve alpha, geometry, unaffected atlas regions, animation objects, and frame records; save as a new version; and require human acceptance on the project-bound live Sprite Lab route.

For one character project, preview every animation with one canonical project-wide pixels-to-screen scale derived from the maximum dimension across all project frames (or an explicitly locked camera scale). Never recompute fit-to-box scale per animation. Preserve atlas pixels and frame rectangles; presentation scale is viewer state, not sprite correction. Add a regression test proving scale is animation-order-independent and identical for compact and wide clips.

Treat browser asset revisions as a dependency-graph contract. When an ES-module export or import changes, version the top-level script and every changed transitive import together, then test that the HTML script revision and imported-module revision match. A healthy API and HTTP 200 are insufficient; verify client startup reaches populated media state.

Use Git as the only source-code transport between authoring and the phone runtime: inspect the authoritative repository and branch, commit the bounded change, push it, then have Phone Hands fetch and fast-forward to the exact commit before phone-local tests, restart, and runtime readback. Phone Hands carries bounded Git/runtime commands and receipts, never source patches, heredocs, or Base64 chunks. Bind the receipt to previous HEAD, pulled SHA, clean/dirty status, test result, and served asset revision. If the live runtime is not a Git checkout, establish a Git-backed checkout or deterministic deployment from one; keep phone-local project JSON and accepted atlas data outside source transport unless the repository explicitly governs them.
